analysis_summary: The log set consists primarily of Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) bind and connection events (EventIDs 5156, 5158) from Azure guest agents and svchost.exe, Sysmon process access and image load events, and a large number of registry modifications related to Delivery Optimization and system environment keys. All observed activities align with normal behavior of Azure virtual machines (metadata service calls) and standard Windows services. No evidence of encoded PowerShell commands, lateral movement, credential dumping, or other malicious techniques was found.
reasoning: 1. Identified the log types: WFP (EventID 5156/5158), Sysmon (EventID 7, 10, 13, 12), and Windows Security Auditing (EventIDs 4656, 4658, 4663, 4690). 2. Normal baseline activities were established: Azure VMs regularly contact 168.63.129.16 (metadata service) and use Delivery Optimization registry keys for bandwidth management. 3. Reviewed each event for anomalies: repetitive bind events from svchost.exe are typical for services listening on multiple ports; registry writes under HKU\S-1-5-20\...\DeliveryOptimization are standard configuration changes; handle duplication and close events for the computer account are routine for system processes accessing environment variables. 4. No suspicious PowerShell -enc strings or other obfuscation were present, so the decoder tool was not required. 5. Event IDs 5156 and 5158 were validated using the event_id_extractor tool. 6. Event IDs 4656, 4658, 4663, and 4690 were also validated using the event_id_extractor tool (all confirmed as correct). 7. No coordinated attack patterns emerged from timeline analysis, confirming benign activity.
